newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt calls confidence vote on Albania decree.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt calls confidence vote on Albania decree.

text.p: The Italian government on Wednesday called a confidence vote in the lower house of parliament to push through a decree on measures to handle thousands of refugees from Albania.

Interior Minister Giorgio Napolitano told parliament he was calling the vote to overcome obstructive tactics by the separatist Northern League. The decree has already been approved by the upper house of parliament.

Italy is leading a U.N.-backed force with a three-month mandate to oversee the secure delivery of humanitarian aid to Albania and earlier on Wednesday called an international conference on the Balkan country in Rome next month.

Italy has been swamped by more than 15,000 refugees who have crossed the Adriatic sea in a flotilla of ramshackle boats to escape anarchy and a growing political crisis ahead of planned elections at home.
Rome declared a national "state of emergency" on March 19, recognising at the time that it had been overwhelmed by the flood and providing measures to cope with the problem.
Under a constitutional court ruling, decrees passed by cabinet must be approved by parliament within 60 days or lapse. The deadline was due to expire on Monday.

The vote was expected to be held on Thursday evening, the same day that international mediator Franz Vranitzky was due in Tirana for his second mission in a week after most political parties threatened to boycott planned June 29 elections.
The Italian Foreign Ministry said Vranitzky would also make a stopover in Rome on Thursday afternoon to discuss the situation with Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi spoke to Vranitzky on Thursday as well as Albanian President Sali Berisha and Prime Minister Bashkim Fino, his office said in a statement.
It said the conversations were aimed at easing the "return to and maintenance of a climate of full political co-existence in Albania" ahead of the planned elections.

Early elections in Albania have been planned since March when Berisha agreed to share power and installed a unity government at the height of unrest which swept the country after the failure of dubious savings schemes.
The threatened boycott would make a mockery of the election just a year after the Socialist Party pulled out of the last vote in May 1996, which observers said was flawed.
Italy also called on all Albanian political forces to "abstain from any initiative that could complicate the situation and to cooperate closely with the special envoy".
The Foreign Ministry said the international conference on Albania would be attended by more than 30 delegations including the United States.
It said the conference, likely to be at foreign minister level, was planned for June 18 in Rome and would be preceded by a preparatory meeting there on May 26.

A ministry spokesman said senior officials from Albania, all 15 European Union countries, the United States and members of the Italian-led security force in Albania were expected to attend the planning session in two weeks' time.

They would be joined by representatives from the European Commission, the United Nations, the Western European Union military alliance, the Council of Europe, the World Bank, the International Monetary Fund and other financial institutions.
